overview: This chapter follows sixteenth-century Denmark-Norway through astronomy, printing and royal architecture. Tycho Brahe's observatory shows how scientific work depended on buildings, instruments and supporting crafts.

items.text: Under Danish royal patronage, Tycho Brahe built Uraniborg on Hven between 1576 and 1580. The island is now Swedish but was then Danish.
Uraniborg included a printing office and a water mill for making paper. Publishing and material production supported the observatory's work.
Tycho established Stjerneborg in 1584. Sheltered instrument spaces reduced exposure to wind and helped stabilize observations.
Frederik II began rebuilding Kronborg as a Renaissance castle in 1574. Its courtyard, carved sandstone and decorated chapel formed a major royal setting.

sources.title: UNESCO and IAU Astronomy Heritage Portal, Uraniborg and Stellaeburgum
